entries.title: Zeta–gamma Mellin integral

source.provenanceScope: User-supplied image; caption retained; no creator, date, license or surrounding post text inferred.

entries.domain: Ordinary complex s with Re(s)>1; real integration variable t>0 and t^(s-1)=exp((s-1)*log(t)).
entries.formula: zeta(s)*Gamma(s) = integral_0^infinity t^(s-1)/(exp(t)-1) dt, for Re(s)>1.

parsedEquations.meaning: Mellin integral identity and its convergence half-plane.
parsedEquations.qualification: The unchanged integral diverges near zero when Re(s)<=1; analytic continuation requires a different representation.

entries.finding: The displayed identity and convergence condition agree with NIST DLMF 25.5.1.
entries.evidence: The small-t integrand behaves as t^(s-2), and the large-t tail decays exponentially. A finite cutoff/quadrature and transformed sampled integrand are bounded numerical profiles. They are not finite-field zeta/Gamma functions and do not retain the improper-integral identity by a Fourier round trip.
